Overview of the Cambridge Assessment English A2 Key Reading and Writing
Paper – Teacher’s Notes

Description

To familiarise students with the content of the A2 Key Reading and Writing paper

Time required:  45 minutes
Materials
required:        download a sample Reading and Writing paper (one per student) from
                     the Cambridge English website
Aims:
                 Student handout (one per student)
                 Answer key (one copy for each small group of students)

                 to familiarise students with the A2 Key Reading and Writing paper
                
                

Procedure

    1. Before the class, prepare one copy of the sample paper from the handbook for each student.
         You can download this from the free resources on the Cambridge English website.

2. Write the following words on the board. Check students understand the meaning of the words
    and ask which they think will be tested in A2 Key

Reading skills Writing skills Spelling Grammar Functional English Vocabulary

3. Explain to your students that the A2 Key Reading and Writing paper tests all of these areas,
    and that they are now going to look at a sample paper to find out more about the test. Explain
    that they don’t need to do the tasks; they just need to look at them and answer the questions
    about them.
    Timing: 5 mins

4. Give students the sample paper and the Student handout. Ask students to work in pairs and
    answer questions 1-3. (See Answer key)
    Timing: 7 mins

5. Go over the answers as a class then refer to the words on the board again. Ask them: Which
    part tests Reading skills? Go through all the areas like this.

Answers
    Reading skills: Part 1, Part 2 and Part 3
    Writing skills: Part 6 and Part 7
    Spelling: Part 5, Part 6 and Part 7
    Grammar: Part 6 and Part 7
    Functional Language: Part 1 and Part 5
    Vocabulary: Part 4 and Part 5
    (Students may have alternative answers to the above and these may be correct – for example
    knowledge of vocabulary and grammar is important for all parts even if it is not being directly
    tested.)
    Timing: 5 mins

6. Ask students to work in pairs again and complete section 2 of the handout. Go over the answers
    with the whole class. (See Answer key)
    Timing: 7 mins

7. Divide the class into three groups: A, B and C. Students don’t need to move, they just need to
    know which letter they are. Explain that they are going to look at the topics that they may find on
    the paper. Ask them to work individually to do section 3 of the handout. Explain that they can
    choose more than one topic for each part.
    Timing: 5 mins

8. Ask students to stand up and to make new groups of three. Each group should include an A,
    a B and a C. They should share their answers from section 3 with one another.
    Timing: 5 mins

9. Go over the answers with students. Explain that all the topics on the test will be familiar to
    them and within their normal experiences. (See Answer key)
    Timing: 3 mins

10. Put students into small groups, give each one an answer sheet, and let them practise
    completing it using a pencil, not a pen. Remind them that when they take the Reading and
    Writing paper, they do not have extra time at the end to transfer their answer from the
    question paper to the answer sheet.
    Timing: 3 mins

11. Answer any questions your students may have about the A2 Key Reading and Writing paper.
    Timing: 5 mins

Student handout

Section 1

1. How many parts are there in the Cambridge English: Key Reading and Writing paper?

2. How many questions are there?

3. How much time do you have to do the paper?

4. In which part (or parts) do you read:

a. some signs and notices?                             f. simplified encyclopedias?

b. packaging information?                              g. leaflets and brochures?

c. an email?                                           h. websites?

d. an article from a newspaper, magazine or website?

e. a text message?

Section 2
In which part do you have to:

   a. choose the best item of vocabulary to complete a sentence?
   b. write a story?
   c. match a question to one of the texts?
   d. choose the best grammar word to complete a text?
   e. write an email?
   f. choose the sentence that matches the meaning of the text?
   g. choose a sentence that answers the question?

Section 3
Topics you can find in Cambridge English: Key Reading and Writing

Clothes                           Daily life                       Entertainment and media
                                                                   House and home
Food and drink                    Health, medicine and exercise    Personal identification
                                                                   Places and buildings
Languages                         People                           Services
                                                                   The natural world
Personal feelings, opinions and experiences                        Weather

School and study                  Shopping

Social interaction                Sport

Transport                         Travel and holidays

Student A
Look at Parts 1 and 2 of the sample paper. Match them to the topics from the list.

Student B
Look at Parts 3 and 4 of the sample paper. Match them to the topics from the list.
